item.title: Misata Introduces Declarative Synthetic Data Generation with Verification
item.description:
Misata Introduces Declarative Synthetic Data Generation with Verification

Misata is a new declarative synthetic data generator for Python. It allows developers to write down the facts a dataset must satisfy, and the engine builds multi-table data that satisfies all of them simultaneously.

🧩 How it works

Users define invariants in a misata.yaml file, such as monthly revenue curves, balanced ledgers, or foreign key constraints. The system generates rows derived from these specifications.

  • Specification as Ground Truth: The specification is the ground truth, and the rows are derived from it. For example, if the specification states “January revenue is 180,000,” this is true before a single row exists.
  • DuckDB Integration: Once data is generated, DuckDB checks the files on disk and writes a certificate that anyone can re-run.
  • Independent Verification: The verify.py script uses only the standard library and duckdb. It shares no code with the generator.

⚙️ Key details

The tool addresses the “oracle problem” in testing, where verifying data pipelines requires both input data and an independently known answer. Traditional methods have limitations:

  • Copying Production: Provides data without a known answer.
  • Hand-written Fixtures: Provide an answer that rots.
  • Random Generators: Provide data whose answer must be computed by the code under test.

In a documented example, Misata generated data satisfying 69 invariants, including:

  • Twelve monthly revenue totals (e.g., 180,000.00 in January, 240,000.00 in June).
  • Channel splits inside each month.
  • Planned row counts per month.
  • Zero orphaned customer_ids and unique keys.

The verification process can detect specific failures, such as a mismatched SHA256 hash or a precision error where an observed value of 180000.01 does not match the expected 180000.00.

🚀 Availability

Misata is available for Python. It can be installed and used as follows:

1
2
3
4
5
6
7
8

# Installation
pip install "misata[duckdb]"

# Data Generation
misata generate -c misata.yaml -o data --attest

# Verification
python data/verify.py

A successful verification outputs a certificate indicating that files match their attested SHA256 hashes and all invariants hold.

#SyntheticData #Python #DataEngineering #Testing #DuckDB

item.title: Mostly AI engine enables flexible tabular and text model reuse
item.description:
Mostly AI engine enables flexible tabular and text model reuse

🔍 Overview

A new library, mostlyai-engine, serves as the core model engine for the Mostly AI Synthetic Data SDK. It allows users to train models on flat or sequential data and flexibly reuse them for various downstream tasks without retraining. The engine supports two primary model classes: TabularARGN for structured tabular data and LanguageModel for semi-structured textual tabular data.

🧩 How it works

The TabularARGN class provides a scikit-learn-compatible interface for working with structured, flat, or sequential tabular data. Once trained, models can be reused for regression, classification, imputation, and sampling. Key training and generation capabilities include:

  • Control training time and parameters
  • Monitor training progress
  • Optionally enable differential privacy
  • Optionally provide context data
  • Up-sample or down-sample
  • Conditionally generate
  • Rebalance categories
  • Impute missing values
  • Incorporate fairness

⚙️ Key details

The library supports synthetic data generation, classification, regression, and imputation through a few lines of Python code. Users can load data, train the model, and perform tasks such as:

  • Generating new synthetic samples
  • Generating new synthetic samples conditionally
  • Filling in missing values
  • Predicting categorical or numerical target columns
  • Assessing marginal conditional probability for one or more target columns

A companion tool, mostlyai-qa, is used to assess the fidelity and novelty of synthetic samples with respect to original samples. It calculates accuracy, similarity, and distance metrics, visualizes statistics for comparison against training and holdout samples, and generates a standalone HTML summary report. It supports analyzing single-table data, sequential data, and sequential data with context.

🚀 Availability

The latest release of mostlyai-engine can be installed via uv. It is highly recommended to install the package within a dedicated virtual environment. For GPU setups required for LLM finetuning and inference, specific installation instructions are provided. On Linux, users can explicitly install the CPU-only variant of PyTorch together with mostlyai-engine. The mostlyai-qa package is available via pip install -U mostlyai-qa.

#SyntheticData #TabularAI #ModelReuse #MostlyAI #Python

Source: mostly-ai/mostlyai-engine Source: mostly-ai/mostlyai-qa

item.title: TRDG Adds Non‑Latin Text Support for Synthetic OCR Data
item.description:
TRDG Adds Non‑Latin Text Support for Synthetic OCR Data

A new update to the Text Recognition Data Generator (TRDG) introduces synthetic data generation for non‑Latin scripts, expanding its utility for OCR training.

🔍 Overview

  • TRDG creates text‑image samples to train OCR software.
  • The latest release adds support for Simplified and Traditional Chinese as well as Japanese.
  • Generated texts are available in both Chinese scripts.

🧩 How It Works

  • Run the tool from the command line after installing the trdg package.
  • Example commands:
    • trdg -l cn -c 1000 -w 5 – generate 1,000 Chinese images.
    • trdg -l ja -c 1000 -w 5 – generate 1,000 Japanese images.
  • Use the -or flag to change text orientation and -tc '#000000,#FFFFFF' to set a color range.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Installation: pip install trdg (recommended inside a virtualenv).
  • Alternative install: Clone the repo and run pip install -r requirements.txt to add new languages.
  • Docker: docker pull belval/trdg:latest then docker run -v /output/path/:/app/out/ -t belval/trdg:latest trdg [args] (output path must be absolute).
  • Customisation options:
    • --stroke_width – set text stroke width.
    • --stroke_fill – set stroke colour (requires stroke_width > 0).
    • --word_split – split on words instead of characters.
    • --dict – specify a custom dictionary.
    • --font_dir – point to a directory of fonts.
    • --font – use a single font for all images.
    • --output_mask – output a character‑level mask per image.
    • --character_spacing – adjust pixel spacing between characters.
    • --fit and --margins – finer layout control.

🚀 Availability

  • The package is available on PyPI (pip install trdg).
  • Docker image: belval/trdg:latest.
  • Source code can be cloned for further language extensions.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Synthetic data reduces the need for costly manual annotation.
  • Adding Chinese and Japanese expands OCR research and commercial applications into Asian markets.
  • Flexible CLI arguments let users tailor datasets to specific model requirements.

📊 Language Support Table

Language Scripts Supported Example CLI
Chinese Simplified, Traditional trdg -l cn -c 1000 -w 5
Japanese — trdg -l ja -c 1000 -w 5

item.title: GraphGen Initial Release Adds Knowledge-Guided Synthetic Data for LLMs
item.description:
GraphGen Initial Release Adds Knowledge-Guided Synthetic Data for LLMs

The initial version of GraphGen has been released, a framework designed for synthetic data generation guided by knowledge graphs. It constructs fine-grained knowledge graphs from source text and identifies knowledge gaps in Large Language Models (LLMs) using the expected calibration error metric, prioritizing QA pairs that target high-value, long-tail knowledge. The associated paper, “Knowledge-to-Verification: Exploring RLVR for LLMs in Knowledge-Intensive Domains,” has been accepted to the ACL 2026 Main Conference.

🧩 How it works

GraphGen operates by first constructing a fine-grained knowledge graph from the source text. It then identifies knowledge gaps in LLMs using the expected calibration error metric, which allows it to prioritize the generation of QA pairs that target high-value, long-tail knowledge. The framework incorporates multi-hop neighborhood sampling to capture complex relational information and employs style-controlled generation to diversify the resulting QA data. Additionally, support for community detection in knowledge graphs using the Leiden algorithm enables the synthesis of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) data.

⚙️ Key details

GraphGen supports a range of input sources and data formats, including HuggingFace Datasets and PDF files processed via MinerU. It also supports Visual Question Answering (VQA) data generation. The framework includes knowledge graph evaluation metrics covering:

  • Accuracy (entity/relation)
  • Consistency (conflict detection)
  • Structural robustness (noise, connectivity, degree distribution)

The backend infrastructure includes support for rocksdb as a key-value storage backend and kuzudb as a graph database backend. Local inference is supported via vllm. For distributed execution and resource management, the data generation pipeline has been refactored using Ray.

🔌 Integration and Clients

After data generation, users can fine-tune their LLMs using LLaMA-Factory and xtuner. GraphGen supports several new LLM clients and inference backends:

Component Function/Details
Ollama_client Supported LLM client
http_client Supported LLM client
HuggingFace Transformers Supported inference backend
SGLang Supported inference backend
vllm Local inference backend

Search support has been added for several back-ends and databases, enabling the extraction of specific data types:

  • Google, Bing, and Wikipedia search back-ends.
  • UniProt, NCBI, and RNAcentral databases for extracting DNA and RNA data from bioinformatics sources.

📈 Data Modalities

LLM benchmark synthesis within GraphGen supports multiple question formats, which is ideal for education:

  • Single-choice
  • Multiple-choice
  • Fill-in-the-blank
  • True-or-false

🚀 Availability

The initial version of GraphGen is available with auto-updating Gradio demos hosted on Hugging Face and ModelScope.

#GraphGen #KnowledgeGraphs #SyntheticData #LLMTraining #ACL2026

Source: InternScience/GraphGen

item.title: DeepFabric generates synthetic data for language model training
item.description:
DeepFabric generates synthetic data for language model training

DeepFabric is a tool designed to generate synthetic training data for language models and agent evaluations. It combines reasoning traces with tool-calling patterns to create high-quality, domain-specific datasets that teach models to think, plan, and act effectively, call tools correctly, and conform to strict schema structures.

🔍 Overview

The system distinguishes itself through unique topic graph generation algorithms that ensure high diversity while maintaining domain-anchored relevance. This approach guides sample creation to cover all necessary subtopics while avoiding redundancy, a common issue in other tools that can lead to model overfitting.

🧩 How it works

  • Data Generation: The process involves constrained decoding and response validation.
  • Tool Execution: Real tool executions occur within isolated webassembly environments.
  • Accuracy: These mechanisms ensure generated samples strictly adhere to structured schemas, variable constraints, and execution correctness, providing exact syntax and structure for training pipelines.
  • Tool Definitions: Tool definitions can be imported directly from MCP (Model Context Protocol) server schemas, automatically mocked, or based on real-life interfaces.
  • Standard Tools: A standard set of common tools, such as list_files() and read_file(), is included.

⚙️ Key details

  • Deployment Options: DeepFabric can be used as a library, a CLI tool, or via YAML configuration.
  • Configuration: The YAML configuration includes three main sections and optional shared LLM defaults.
  • Mocked Execution: Using mocked tool execution requires a running Spin service, which is provided in a Docker image.
  • Example Output: A specific configuration generated a topic graph with 27 unique nodes, resulting in 27 training samples saved to dataset.jsonl and achieving 100% topic coverage.

🚀 Availability

  • Integration: Generated datasets can be automatically uploaded to Hugging Face.
  • Training Frameworks: Data can be directly imported into popular training frameworks, including TRL, Unsloth, and Axolotl.
  • Evaluation: A built-in evaluation engine assesses model performance on unseen tasks derived from training splits, covering evaluation-only questions, answers, and tool traces.

#DeepFabric #SyntheticData #LLMTraining #AgentEvaluations #MCP #HuggingFace

Source: nolabs-ai/deepfabric

item.title: DeepEcho Pre-Alpha Library Generates Synthetic Time Series Data
item.description:
DeepEcho Pre-Alpha Library Generates Synthetic Time Series Data

DataCebo’s Synthetic Data Vault Project has released DeepEcho, a Python library for generating synthetic mixed-type multivariate time series data. The library is currently in Pre-Alpha stage and available both as part of the SDV ecosystem and as a standalone package.

🔍 Overview

  • DeepEcho is a Synthetic Data Generation Python library for mixed-type, multivariate time series
  • Part of The Synthetic Data Vault Project from DataCebo
  • Automatically installed alongside SDV, but can also be used independently
  • Software is in its Pre-Alpha stage

🧩 Key Features

  • Multiple models based on classical statistical modeling and the latest Deep Learning techniques
  • Robust benchmarking framework for evaluating methods on multiple datasets with multiple metrics
  • API for Machine Learning researchers to submit new methods following the model and sample interface
  • Regular publishing of useful content about Synthetic Data Generation
  • Documentation includes Quickstarts, User and Development Guides, and API Reference

⚙️ Installation Options

Via SDV (recommended)

  • DeepEcho is part of the SDV project and automatically installed alongside it
  • Provides additional functionalities not available in standalone version
  • See SDV Installation Guide for details

Standalone Installation

  • pip install deepecho
  • conda install -c pytorch -c conda-forge deepecho

🚀 Usage Example

The quickstart demonstrates learning a mixed-type multivariate time series dataset:

1
2
3

model = PARModel(cuda=False)
# Or with custom settings
model = PARModel(epochs=1024, cuda=True)

Note: For smaller datasets, CUDA usage introduces more overhead than gains from parallelization, making the process more efficient without CUDA.

Workflow:

  1. Load data and prepare model instance
  2. Define data types for all columns
  3. Learn a model from the data
  4. Generate new synthetic data that resembles it

💡 Community & Resources

  • SDV Website for project information
  • GitHub Repository available
  • Slack Workspace for announcements and discussions
  • SDV Tutorials runnable in Binder environment
  • User Guide for DeepEcho within SDV

#SyntheticData #TimeSeries #Python #DataGeneration #DataCebo #SDV

item.title: EyeDiT: Advancing 3D Eye Generation for AR/VR Applications
item.description:
EyeDiT: Advancing 3D Eye Generation for AR/VR Applications

Synthetic eye data are critical for rapid development of eye tracking (ET) in AR/VR applications. However, existing synthetic eye generators are largely image-centric and lack a high-quality underlying 3D anatomy of the eye, which limits their control mainly to the gaze and provides no anatomical labels.

🔍 Overview

  • Synthetic eye data are critical for rapid development of eye tracking (ET) in AR/VR applications.
  • Existing synthetic eye generators are largely image-centric and lack a high-quality underlying 3D anatomy of the eye.

🧩 How it works

  • EyeDiT is an anatomy-grounded, multi-modal 3D eye generation and simulation model trained with optical coherence tomography (OCT), labeled anatomy point clouds and near-eye images.
  • The pipeline first trains a Multi-Modal Anatomy Variational Autoencoder (VAE), which encodes an anatomy-aware latent representation from all input modalities.
  • Then, Eye Latent DiT is trained to generate latent samples conditioned on the optical axis, the pupil position and radius, and the subject identity.
  • The model enables control over the pupil, subject identity and viewpoint for data synthesis.

⚙️ Key details

  • The model outperforms previous eye image synthesis models in novel-view synthesis (24.9 against 21.8 dB PSNR from a single view).
  • A public ET neural network trained on EyeDiT’s synthetic data shows a smaller sim-to-real gap than when trained on data from other generators (3.5° vs. 8.4° gaze error).
  • The network approaches a network trained on real data, and further improves ET performance when combined with real data (2.3° vs. 2.6°).

🚀 Availability

  • More information is available on the project page: EyeDiT Project Page

💡 Why it matters

  • EyeDiT addresses the limitations of existing synthetic eye generators by providing a high-quality underlying 3D anatomy of the eye.
  • The model enables control over the pupil, subject identity and viewpoint for data synthesis, which is critical for rapid development of eye tracking (ET) in AR/VR applications.
  • The model outperforms previous eye image synthesis models and shows a smaller sim-to-real gap when used to train a public ET neural network.

#EyeTracking #ARVR #SyntheticData #3DEyeGeneration

Source: EyeDiT: Anatomy-Grounded Multi-Modal Eye Generation and Simulation

item.title: NVIDIA Releases Cosmos3-Edge and Cosmos Data Factory for Physical AI Development
item.description:
NVIDIA Releases Cosmos3-Edge and Cosmos Data Factory for Physical AI Development

NVIDIA has released Cosmos3-Edge, a 4B parameter model tier optimized for on-device, real-time deployment on Jetson AGX Orin, Thor, and RTX Pro 6000. This follows the release of Cosmos 3, an open platform of world models, datasets, frameworks, and tools designed to enable physical AI applications across robotics, autonomous vehicles, smart infrastructure, manufacturing, healthcare, and agriculture.

🔍 Overview

NVIDIA Cosmos is an open platform developed to provide physical AI developers with better data, a better environment, a better starting point, and better tooling. The underlying Cosmos 3 model family is built on a unified Mixture-of-Transformers architecture. These omnimodal world models are capable of seeing, reasoning, simulating, and acting, allowing them to render physical momentum, perform forward dynamics, and reason in complex real-world scenarios.

🛠️ Cosmos Data Factory Blueprints

As part of this platform, NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory (CDF) provides five cloud-native blueprints and six composable skills to accelerate data curation, processing, and synthetic data generation (SDG). AI agents can orchestrate these blueprints for prompt-to-data workflows without human steering.

Blueprint Function Key Components Used
Autonomous Vehicle Dataset Generation Searches databases of driving scenarios and generates novel datasets for model training and validation. Cosmos Curator, Dataset Search, Cosmos3-Super-Image2Video, Cosmos Evaluator
Image Attribute Augmentation Generates variations of person-crops with controlled changes to attributes like clothing, accessories, and color. LLM, Cosmos Evaluator
Video Data Augmentation Transforms existing footage across weather, lighting, and environmental conditions while preserving scene structure. VLM, Cosmos3-Nano, Cosmos Evaluator
Event Video Generation Uses a source image to create videos of rare events like fires, falls, or shoplifting. VLM, Cosmos3-Super-Image2Video, Cosmos Evaluator

⚙️ Key details

The workflows and blueprints within Cosmos Data Factory are powered by several core tools and skills:

  • CDF Orchestration Core Skill: Coordinates workflow steps, deploys required services, and manages execution on your cluster.
  • Preflight and Setup: Preflight checks the cluster environment without making changes to flag missing components, while setup configures the environment to run the blueprints.
  • NVIDIA Cosmos Curator: Extracts metadata for video dataset inputs, and works with Cosmos Dataset Search to locate relevant videos through embeddings.
  • Cosmos Evaluator: Reviews generated content to verify the requested attributes or conditions appear, and evaluates whether motion is physically plausible without artifacts.
  • Cosmos Framework: Provides training infrastructure supporting supervised fine-tuning (SFT), LoRA, reinforcement learning (RL), and distillation.

🚀 Availability

  • Cosmos 3: Released in May 2026, comprising the unified Mixture-of-Transformers model family.
  • Cosmos3-Edge: Released in July 2026, offering a 4B parameter tier for on-device, real-time deployment on Jetson AGX Orin, Thor, and RTX Pro 6000 hardware platforms.

#NVIDIA #Cosmos #PhysicalAI #SyntheticData #Robotics

Source: Build Training-Ready Physical AI Datasets with Two Prompts in NVIDIA Cosmos | NVIDIA Technical Blog Source: NVIDIA/cosmos

item.title: OfficePrism Benchmarks 420 Enterprise Tasks Across Business Functions
item.description:
OfficePrism Benchmarks 420 Enterprise Tasks Across Business Functions

OfficePrism has been introduced as an evaluation framework designed to assess AI performance in enterprise environments. The system addresses the difficulty of localizing failures when broad workplace scores mix competence within a single business function with the costs of coordinating across multiple functions and systems. To resolve this, OfficePrism evaluates prerequisites through a structured set of tasks that isolate specific domains while maintaining shared organizational context.

🔍 Overview

The framework is built to test models on realistic enterprise workflows. It moves beyond generic benchmarks by using a shared synthetic organization that defines the context for each test case. This approach allows for a clearer distinction between functional competence and coordination overhead.

🧩 How it works

The evaluation pipeline constructs test scenarios using grounded records, business rules, and tool schemas. This process jointly creates:

  • A Chinese-language ticket
  • A hidden executable reference witness
  • An expected response

Each of the 420 single-domain enterprise tasks is executed in a fresh environment. This environment combines the shared synthetic organization with one function-specific domain and typed state access. The tasks are filtered automatically and curated by humans before inclusion in the final set. The evaluation spans seven business functions and uses three benchmark-defined task-structure levels: L1, L2, and L3.

⚙️ Key details

The same task set is evaluated using two different configuration packages: full-schema and search-and-dispatch. The results across 124 model-harness-package configurations show significant variance in performance:

Metric Result
Per-case joint pass rate range 22.6% to 76.4%
Median pass rate 67.9%
L1 performance Highest in all 124 configurations
L2 vs. L3 performance L2 exceeds L3 in 122 out of 124 configurations

When comparing configurations that share the same harness and model labels across both packages, the search-and-dispatch package scored higher in 30 instances, tied in one, and scored lower in 19 instances compared to the full-schema package.

#OfficePrism #AIBenchmarking #EnterpriseAI #LLMEvaluation #SyntheticData

Source: OfficePrism: Benchmarking Agents on Single-Domain Operations Across Enterprise Business Functions

item.title: Community members step in to maintain Distilabel synthetic data framework
item.description:
Community members step in to maintain Distilabel synthetic data framework

The original authors of Distilabel, a framework for synthetic data and AI feedback, have moved on to other projects. In response, a group of community members has recently joined the GitHub project as collaborators to maintain it and are actively working towards the next release. In the meantime, users can check out the develop branch for access to the latest fixes and improvements.

🔍 Overview

Distilabel is an open-source, community-driven framework designed for engineers who need fast, reliable, and scalable pipelines based on verified research papers. Its goal is to accelerate AI development by quickly generating high-quality, diverse datasets for synthesizing and judging data using AI feedback. By focusing on data quality, Distilabel aims to tackle the root causes of expensive compute and output quality issues, allowing users to spend their time achieving high-quality standards.

🧩 How it works

Distilabel uses a programmatic approach to build scalable pipelines for data generation and AI feedback. It integrates AI feedback from any LLM provider using one unified API, ensuring flexibility, scalability, and fault tolerance while leveraging the latest research papers.

💡 Why it matters

The framework helps users synthesize and judge data for a wide variety of projects, including:

  • Traditional predictive NLP (classification, extraction).
  • Generative and large language model scenarios (instruction following, dialogue generation, judging).
  • Ownership of data for fine-tuning custom LLMs.

The Argilla community uses distilabel to create datasets and models, such as:

  • The 1M OpenHermesPreference, a dataset of ~1 million AI preferences derived from teknium/OpenHermes-2.5, demonstrating large-scale data synthesis.
  • The distilabeled Intel Orca DPO dataset and improved OpenHermes model, which show performance improvements by filtering out 50% of the original dataset through AI feedback.
  • The haiku DPO data, which outlines how anyone can create a specific task dataset using the latest research papers to improve quality.

⚙️ Key details

Component/Integration Description
Python Requirement Requires Python 3.9+
anthropic For using models available in Anthropic API via the AnthropicLLM integration.
cohere For using models available in Cohere via the CohereLLM integration.
argilla For exporting the generated datasets to Argilla.
groq For using models available in Groq using groq Python client via the GroqLLM integration.
hf-inference-endpoints For using the Hugging Face Inference Endpoints via the InferenceEndp

#Distilabel #SyntheticData #LLM #OpenSource #AIEngineering

Source: argilla-io/distilabel

item.title: Tabular Foundation Models Advance with Pretrained Transformers and Synthetic Data
item.description:
Tabular Foundation Models Advance with Pretrained Transformers and Synthetic Data

Open with one short intro paragraph stating what happened. Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) have emerged as a transformative approach to handling tabular data, leveraging pretrained transformer architectures to enable predictions on new datasets without task-specific training. These models, developed through synthetic data pretraining, eliminate the need for bespoke training pipelines while offering scalable solutions for complex data relationships.

🔍 Overview

  • TFMs are pretrained on synthetic datasets to infer variable relationships in unseen data.
  • They require no dataset-specific training, reducing overhead for maintaining custom models.
  • Prediction occurs via in-context learning (ICL), using a single forward pass with labeled rows as context.
  • Fine-tuning on specific datasets can further boost accuracy for critical use cases.

🧩 How it works

  • Input Handling: Specialized tokenizers map mixed data types (numerical, categorical, boolean) into a shared latent space.
  • Attention Mechanisms: Sequential row and column attention capture feature interactions but face scalability challenges.
  • Compression: TabICLv1 uses row compression (4 tokens per row) to reduce computational costs.
  • Pretraining: Synthetic data simulates real-world issues like missing values and outliers.

⚙️ Key details

Model Variant Contribution
TabPFNv2 First TFM to scale sequential row/column attention mechanisms.
TabICLv1 Introduced row compression for cost-effective cross-sample attention.
TabPFNv3, TabFM, KumoTabular Top-ranked models in benchmarks like TabArena, building on TabICLv1.
  • Synthetic data generation relies on Structural Causal Models but varies per TFM.
  • Computational costs grow rapidly with large datasets due to dense attention.

🚀 Availability

  • Integrated with Databricks workflows for managed GPU access and fine-tuning.
  • Check benchmarks like TabArena or TALENT for performance comparisons.

💡 Why it matters

  • Eliminates time-consuming model training and retraining cycles.
  • Enables rapid predictions via ICL without dataset-specific setup.
  • Advances transformer applications to tabular data, a historically under-explored domain.

#TabularData #AIModels #Transformers #SyntheticData

Source: Tabular foundation models on Databricks AI Runtime

item.title: SDGym Benchmarking Framework Released for Synthetic Data Evaluation
item.description:
SDGym Benchmarking Framework Released for Synthetic Data Evaluation

The Synthetic Data Vault Project from DataCebo has introduced SDGym (Synthetic Data Gym), a benchmarking framework designed to model and generate synthetic data. This tool allows developers to measure performance, memory usage, and data quality across various modeling techniques, including classical statistics and deep learning.

🔍 Overview

SDGym integrates with the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) ecosystem, providing a way to evaluate synthesizers, datasets, and metrics. The project traces its origins to MIT’s Data to AI Lab in 2016, with DataCebo founded in 2020 to grow the ecosystem, which is now described as the largest for synthetic data generation and evaluation.

🧩 How it works

The framework allows users to benchmark techniques by selecting synthesizers and baselines, then running evaluations on publicly available or custom datasets. Key workflow steps include:

  • Defining which modeling techniques to use, such as GaussianCopulaSynthesizer and CTGANSynthesizer.
  • Selecting baselines, such as UniformSynthesizer.
  • Executing the benchmark using the function sdgym.benchmark_single_table.
  • Generating a detailed evaluation of performance, memory, and quality across the selected datasets.

Users can also customize the process by writing their own machine learning models, specifying training and sampling logic to test personal synthetic data generation techniques.

⚙️ Key details

  • Metrics: Measures performance, memory usage, synthetic data quality, and privacy.
  • Data Sources: Supports publicly available datasets from the SDV project and custom private datasets stored locally or on Amazon S3.
  • Customization: Allows users to include their own synthesizers, datasets, or metrics.
  • Installation: Available via pip or conda, with a recommendation to use a virtual environment to avoid software conflicts.

🚀 Availability

SDGym is part of the SDV library ecosystem. Developers can access the documentation and install the package to begin benchmarking immediately. The library includes a feature to list available datasets, facilitating quick setup for users wishing to test against standard public data.

#SyntheticData #Benchmarking #DataCebo #MachineLearning #SDGym

Source: sdv-dev/SDGym

item.title: Elith and NVIDIA Release Nemotron-Personas-Finance-Japan Synthetic Dataset
item.description:
Elith and NVIDIA Release Nemotron-Personas-Finance-Japan Synthetic Dataset

🔍 Overview

  • The financial sector faces strict privacy regulations and compliance requirements that limit the use of real‑world data.
  • Developing agentic AI for finance therefore needs synthetic data that mimics demographics, household structures, and asset statuses while avoiding privacy risks.
  • Elith and NVIDIA have released Nemotron-Personas-Finance-Japan, a financial‑domain extension of the open‑source persona dataset Nemotron-Personas-Japan.
  • To our knowledge, it is the first open persona dataset at million‑record scale that pairs Japan’s official statistics with household finance and financial literacy data.

🧩 How it works

  • Built on official Japanese government statistics and public survey data.
  • Generated with NeMo SDG‑PGMs, a probabilistic graphical model framework for statistically grounded synthetic data generation, and NeMo Data Designer, NVIDIA’s enterprise synthetic data generation system.
  • Integrated with the NeMo User Sim framework, allowing instant execution of simulations drawn from diverse, realistic distributions.
  • Text generation is performed by gemma‑4‑31B‑it, a Japanese language model.
  • The generation pipeline supports complex Jinja templating, Pydantic validation, structured outputs, automated retries, and multiple generation back‑ends.

⚙️ Key details

  • Scale: 9 M personas (1 M base records × 9 persona variations) – 50 % more than the original Nemotron‑Personas‑Japan.
  • Fields per record: 50 total → 9 persona fields, 11 persona attributes, 30 contextual fields based on official demographic and labor statistics.
  • Token count: ~1.5 B tokens, including ~750 M persona tokens.
  • Synthetic only: No real individuals are represented; names follow real Japanese naming patterns but are generated from statistical distributions.
  • Rich persona attributes:
    • Education granularity beyond national aggregates.
    • Expanded Occupation categories (e.g., business owners, specialized professions).
    • Life‑stage scenarios such as students, retirees, and periods of unemployment.
    • Household finances and real assets to reflect diverse economic backgrounds.
    • Digital & financial literacy indicators (internet and smartphone usage, financial knowledge).
  • Industry input: Designed with feedback from Sompo Japan, Tokio Marine Holdings, Bank of Fukuoka, Mizuho Financial Group, Meiji Yasuda Life Insurance, and the Financial Data Utilization Association (FDUA).

💡 Why it matters

  • Enables realistic financial AI use cases—such as chatbots, sales‑conversation evaluation, and marketing simulations—without exposing real customer data.
  • Helps the industry meet compliance demands while accelerating AI development cycles.

item.title: Microsoft launches synthetic enterprise evaluation platform for Copilot
item.description:
Microsoft launches synthetic enterprise evaluation platform for Copilot

Microsoft introduced the Industry Evaluation Data Generation Platform, a system that creates full‑scale synthetic enterprise environments for evaluating Microsoft Copilot while preserving privacy.

🔍 Overview

  • Evaluating enterprise AI requires test data that captures reporting structures, project histories, communication patterns, and domain‑specific workflows.
  • Real enterprise data contains sensitive information that cannot be used for evaluation under any circumstances.
  • The platform provides synthetic environments that mimic real business workflows, helping Microsoft find issues that generic benchmarks would miss.
  • Safety and privacy are built into the platform by design, with automated content‑safety checks keeping generated data free of harmful or personally identifiable material.

🧩 How it works

The evaluation strategy is built on three core pillars:

Pillar Description
Synthetic enterprise environments Simulated Microsoft Copilot environments with realistic users, meetings, emails, documents, and organizational structures that replicate the complexity of real organizations without using any customer data. Each simulated workspace is called a “tenant”.
Automated query generation pipelines Rapid, reproducible creation of evaluation datasets through automated pipelines.
Structured quality frameworks Ensure synthetic data meets the bar for meaningful evaluation.

To ensure realism, the synthetic environments are grounded in publicly available data sources:

  • O*NET occupational data calibrates employee roles, responsibilities, and workflow frequencies.
  • Online job postings provide realistic role titles, reporting hierarchies, and departmental compositions.
  • SEC filings inform organizational scale, business‑unit structures, and financial contexts. All sources have been reviewed and approved by Microsoft’s legal and policy organization.

The environments are dynamic, simulating time‑evolving organizations with meeting histories, project timelines, email threads spanning weeks, and natural organizational changes.

⚙️ Key details

  • Every environment is fully synthetic; no customer data is used.
  • Automated content‑safety checks remove harmful or personally identifiable material.
  • Tenants are isolated organizational environments with their own users, data, and configurations.
  • The platform supports industry‑specific scenarios such as clinical trial reviews or portfolio updates.
  • It enables Microsoft to answer two fundamental questions: Is Copilot actually doing what users need? and Can we prove it without ever touching their data?

🚀 Why it matters

  • Millions of knowledge workers rely daily on Microsoft Copilot for drafting documents, summarizing meetings, surfacing information, and accelerating productivity.
  • Healthcare organizations use Copilot to synthesize safety signals, summarize meetings, and extract action items, influencing patient outcomes and regulatory confidence.
  • By providing a realistic, privacy‑preserving evaluation baseline, the platform allows Microsoft to detect issues that generic benchmarks would miss and ensures Copilot works as intended.

In this blog post we walk through the evaluation system—from synthetic environment generation to automated query pipelines—and show how it establishes the first standardized evaluation baseline for Microsoft Copilot.

#MicrosoftCopilot #SyntheticData #AIEvaluation

Source: From synthetic enterprise data evaluations to real Microsoft Copilot AI confidence - Microsoft Research

item.title: Synthetic-to-Real Adaptation Lowers Error on Nepali-English Code-Switched ASR Benchmark
item.description:
Synthetic-to-Real Adaptation Lowers Error on Nepali-English Code-Switched ASR Benchmark

Researchers introduced a new benchmark for Nepali‑English code‑switched speech and a two‑stage synthetic‑to‑real adaptation pipeline that improves automatic speech recognition performance.

🔍 Overview

  • Nepali‑English conversational speech poses severe ASR challenges due to script confusion (mixing Devanagari and Latin) and high error rates at language‑switch points.
  • Collecting and annotating human code‑switched audio is expensive.
  • The authors curated a benchmark of 13,044 spontaneous podcast utterances (15.45 h total), split into 10,214 test and 2,830 development utterances, and audited the data to remove machine‑translation leakages and acoustic loops.

🧩 How it works

  • Stage 1 – Supervised Fine‑Tuning (SFT):
    • Fine‑tunes a multilingual foundation model on 0.95 h of synthetic speech generated by a multi‑speaker, dual‑engine TTS pipeline.
  • Stage 2 – Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO):
    • Applies reinforcement‑style optimization with transcription and script rewards to further adapt the model to real speech.

⚙️ Key results

  • Synthetic SFT reduces Mixed Error Rate (MER) from 23.40 % to 21.52 % (‑1.88 pp) and Switch‑Point Error Rate (SPER) from 35.89 % to 28.77 % (‑7.12 pp).
  • GRPO yields statistically significant tweaks on 173 test utterances (1.69 % of the test set), improving English script confusion (SCR_en) from 6.45 % to 6.36 % (p ≤ 0.001) and SPER to 28.70 % (p = 0.022, clustered).
  • Ablation shows an auxiliary script‑reward term matches MER‑only optimization because synthetic rollout groups have near‑zero script variance.
  • On monolingual benchmarks, SFT improves Nepali MER by 2.71 pp, stabilizing at 18.42 % after GRPO (a 2.38 pp gain over baseline) while keeping English lexical WER nearly unchanged (3.38 % vs. 3.33 %).

🚀 Availability

  • Verified transcripts, timestamps, episode metadata, and reconstruction scripts are publicly released.
  • The paper appears on alphaXiv; code, data, and model assets are accessible through platforms such as DagsHub, Hugging Face, Gotit.pub, ScienceCast, and CatalyzeX Code Finder for Papers.

💡 Why it matters

  • Demonstrates that a small amount of high‑quality synthetic speech can provide the primary cross‑domain transfer to spontaneous human code‑switched audio.
  • Reduces dependence on costly human‑annotated code‑switched corpora while delivering measurable error‑rate improvements.
  • Provides a publicly audited benchmark that can spur further research on multilingual and code‑switched ASR.

#codeSwitching #ASR #syntheticData #NeuralFineTuning

Source: Synthetic-to-Real Code-Switched ASR: A Spontaneous Nepali-English Podcast Benchmark

item.title: Structured and Hierarchical Insight with Privacy (SHIP) Improves Private Data Analysis
item.description:
Structured and Hierarchical Insight with Privacy (SHIP) Improves Private Data Analysis

Extracting insights from textual data while protecting user privacy is increasingly important, and a new method called Structured and Hierarchical Insight with Privacy (SHIP) advances this goal.

🔍 Overview

  • Existing methods produce private insights in diverse forms for different analytical purposes, making their utility difficult to assess and compare.
  • This work formulates differentially private (DP) insights as reusable representations for answering analytical queries, providing a common basis for utility assessment.

🧩 How it works

  • Answering analytical queries requires fine‑grained details and cross‑attribute statistics that existing representations may omit.
  • SHIP automatically maps queries to attributes, builds a hierarchical hybrid taxonomy, and releases a DP synthetic table for further analysis.

Key capabilities

  • Automatic query‑to‑attribute mapping
  • Hierarchical hybrid taxonomy construction
  • Generation of a differentially private synthetic table

⚙️ Evaluation

  • An evaluation protocol is developed, focusing on question‑answering performance and structured fidelity.
  • Experiments show SHIP’s strong performance on both measures relative to existing private insight baselines.
  • The study also identifies queries that remain challenging for structured representations.

💡 Why it matters

  • Protecting privacy while extracting insights is a growing priority.
  • By providing reusable, comparable DP representations, SHIP helps assess utility across methods and improves the quality of privacy‑preserving analysis.

#DifferentialPrivacy #SyntheticData #PrivacyPreservingAI

Source: SHIP: Structured and Hierarchical Insight with Privacy

item.title: Introduction of QVAC Genesis III STEM-Focused Synthetic Corpus
item.description:
Introduction of QVAC Genesis III STEM-Focused Synthetic Corpus

Researchers have introduced QVAC Genesis III, a multi-domain synthetic corpus designed to address the bottleneck of high-quality pre-training data for educational and STEM-specific language models targeting edge AI and on-device deployment.

🔍 Overview

QVAC Genesis III is a 191.43B-token corpus that covers 19 domains. It is designed to provide high per-token learning value for small models across several difficulty levels and different educational styles.

🧩 How it works

The corpus is built using a dual generation strategy that performs targeted teacher distillation using a weak edge-scale student model as a signal:

  • Student Failures: These are converted into corrective explanations.
  • Student Successes: These are expanded into contrastive option-level reasoning over all answer choices.

⚙️ Key details

To evaluate the data, a new LLM-as-a-parser protocol was introduced to track answer validity and extract final answers from free-form outputs. Validation was conducted via controlled from-scratch ablations using 1.7B-parameter models.

Benchmark Performance Result
ARC-E Up to +28.57% improvement
ARC-C Up to +21.35% improvement
Valid Answer Rate Up to 99.45%

💡 Why it matters

Models trained with QVAC Genesis III consistently outperform the publicly released Cosmo-1B model and those trained with the open-source synthetic corpus Cosmopedia-v2 across MMLU STEM, GPQA Diamond, and ARC benchmarks.

#STEM #SyntheticData #EdgeAI #LLM

Source: QVAC Genesis III: A Large-Scale, High-Quality Open Synthetic STEM Corpus for Efficient Language Model Pre-Training Source: Sample Count Is Not Enough: Candidate-Generation Strategy Shapes the Energy and Performance of LLM Test-Time Scaling Source: LSTM-UT and Recurrent-Depth Transformers on Cellular Automata Source: Learn Your Own Thoughts: Abstract Token Curriculum

item.title: Synthetic Data Augmentation Pipeline Improves Industrial Safety Person Detection
item.description:
Synthetic Data Augmentation Pipeline Improves Industrial Safety Person Detection

A new end-to-end synthetic data augmentation pipeline has been developed to improve person-detection models for industrial safety AI. The system generates labeled training images to address the scarcity of images showing people in dangerous proximity to heavy machinery.

💡 Why it matters

Industries using autonomous equipment in agriculture, construction, mining, and manufacturing require reliable person-detection models. These models must run on edge devices co-located with equipment—such as cameras on railcars, forklifts, or tractors—which necessitates lightweight architectures where every training example is disproportionately important.

Traditional data collection poses significant challenges:

  • Manual annotation and collection can cost an estimated $3–$5 per image.
  • Scaling is difficult, with annotation teams typically processing around 2,000 images per day.
  • Obtaining images of people in hazardous positions often requires hazardous photography sessions.

🧩 How it works

Rather than generating synthetic scenes from scratch, this approach edits real images that contain equipment but no people.

Component Function
Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 A diffusion-based model that inserts synthetic people into real scenes while preserving lighting, scale, and background.
Amazon SageMaker AI Hosts the diffusion model using an ml.g5.12xlarge instance (4× NVIDIA A10G GPUs, 96 GB total VRAM).
Amazon Rekognition DetectLabels API Automatically generates bounding-box annotations for the inserted people.

The pipeline follows these steps:

  1. Prompting: The model receives a structured prompt specifying a person with randomized gender for demographic diversity, hazardous positioning (e.g., on tracks, hanging from edges, or in a vehicle’s path), and constraints to ensure sharp focus and no distortion.
  2. Labeling: The Rekognition DetectLabels API processes images with a minimum confidence threshold of 80 percent.
  3. Refinement: Bounding boxes are deduplicated using non-maximum suppression (NMS) with an IoU threshold > 0.5 and converted to YOLO format.
  4. Merging: These pseudo-labels are merged with original equipment annotations and combined with real training data.
  5. Automation: Image filtering, resizing, prompt assembly, and label processing are handled as an automated workflow.

⚙️ Key details

Experiments using this pipeline showed up to 160 percent improvement in person detection mAP50 (mean Average Precision at an Intersection over Union threshold of 0.5) without requiring manual annotation or hazardous photography.

#IndustrialSafety #ComputerVision #SyntheticData #AmazonSageMaker #PersonDetection

Source: Enhancing industrial safety AI with synthetic data on Amazon SageMaker AI | Amazon Web Services

item.title: End-to-End Approach for Generating Context-Specific LLM Benchmark Datasets
item.description:
End-to-End Approach for Generating Context-Specific LLM Benchmark Datasets

A new paper presents an end-to-end approach for creating large language model (LLM) benchmark datasets by combining synthetic data generation with expert input.

💡 Why it matters

Existing benchmark construction methods typically face a trade-off between validity and scalability:

  • Expert-designed datasets: Produce high-quality evaluations but are slow and costly to create.
  • Synthetically generated data: Scale efficiently but often result in redundant, unrealistic, or out-of-scope examples.

🧩 How it works

To address these gaps, the approach utilizes the following mechanisms:

  • Schema Elicitation: A schema is used to elicit key information regarding the context, scope, and goals of an evaluation task, which then guides the synthetic data generation.
  • Expert-Informed Scaffolds: These scaffolds guide synthetic generation toward more valid benchmarks.

⚙️ Key details

The researchers defined four criteria grounded in measurement validity to assess dataset quality:

Criterion Purpose
Coverage Assessing dataset quality
Diversity Assessing dataset quality
Content Realism Assessing dataset quality
Stylistic Realism Assessing dataset quality

Through quantitative evaluations and a real-world case study with domain experts, the authors demonstrate that this approach improves benchmark data quality over existing methods while preserving validity. Additionally, the research analyzes how different types of schema information affect specific quality criteria to provide guidance on prioritizing information collection under resource constraints.

#LLM #Benchmarks #SyntheticData #AIevaluation

Source: A Framework for Generating Valid Context-Specific Benchmarks through Expert Guidance
